title: Aqueduct
tagline: A DeFi maker's real risk is every strategy added up, not one trade — we gate live on that number.
description: A DeFi maker's liquidity can look safe strategy-by-strategy while being dangerously overcommitted in aggregate — the "multiplier effect." Aqueduct adds _exposureGate1D, a new SwapVM instruction that reads a maker's live, cross-strategy exposure from an on-chain oracle and derates or halts their fill — monotonic by construction, so it can only ever make a fill more conservative, never better. A Uniswap v4 hook (AquaV4Hook) sources v4 swaps from that exact same gated strategy, so the identical safety guarantee holds on both a direct SwapVM swap and a Uniswap v4 swap — proven bit-for-bit identical on real Base Sepolia transactions. The Graph aggregates the maker's exposure across every strategy they've shipped, feeds the oracle, and re-exposes real swap data in a standardized Messari DEX-AMM schema plus an MCP server so AI agents can query it directly. Every number shown is live on Base Sepolia, independently verified on-chain — not mocked, not simulated.
how_its_made: Built in Foundry against real, unmodified 1inch Aqua/SwapVM and Uniswap v4-core/v4-periphery — no forks, no mocks. _exposureGate1D is appended to stock AquaOpcodes at a fresh index, alongside OraclePriceAdjuster (1inch's own instruction, wired into AquaOpcodes for the first time here) composed into a three-instruction "Strategy P" position reading a real Chainlink ETH/USD feed. On the Uniswap side, we extracted a reusable AsyncLiquidityHook base solving v4's flash-accounting settlement-order problem (a working-capital float: mint claims, fund from the hook's own balance, settle, sweep later) — proven generic with two independent implementations — then added a second, independent v4 capability: a risk-adjusted dynamic LP fee via LPFeeLibrary/updateDynamicLPFee, mirroring OpenZeppelin's uniswap-hooks patterns. The Graph side runs a custom subgraph plus a trimmed Messari DEX-AMM standardized layer (same entity/field names as messari/subgraphs) and a zero-dependency MCP server exposing exposure and safety-verdict tools over stdio. Frontend is Next.js + ethers, reading live contract and subgraph state with no personal RPC key shipped client-side. 49 Foundry tests, including a 128,000-call stateful-fuzz invariant suite proving committed-balance accounting holds under arbitrary sequences of pushes, pauses, and swaps.
